quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Harbor seals, which you can often spot in the Strait of Juan de Fuca, can hold their breath for up to 30 minutes while diving for fish! They're excellent swimmers but also love to 'haul out' onto rocks and beaches to rest and warm up in the sun, just like sunbathers.

short_read.title: How Gardens Help Us Age Gracefully
short_read.teaser: Researchers have found that gardening provides unique benefits for older adults, from gentle exercise to the joy of nurturing living things. This warm article explores why getting your hands in the soil is so good for body and soul.

medium_read.title: The Secret Language of Hungarian Embroidery
medium_read.teaser: Every region of Hungary developed its own distinctive embroidery patterns, creating a visual language that told stories through flowers, colors, and stitches. This fascinating article reveals how these beautiful folk art traditions carried meaning from generation to generation.

long_read.title: The Hidden Life of Old-Growth Forests
long_read.teaser: Scientists studying ancient forests like those in Olympic National Park have discovered that trees communicate and even care for each other through underground fungal networks. This captivating piece explores the secret world beneath the forest floor.

port_angeles.title: Deer Spotting Season Begins
port_angeles.description: Early September is a wonderful time to see black-tailed deer in the meadows around Port Angeles, especially at dawn and dusk. The Hurricane Ridge meadows are particularly good viewing spots as the deer prepare for autumn. Bring binoculars and enjoy watching these graceful animals from a respectful distance!

puzzle_1.question: A black-tailed deer's antlers can grow up to ___ inches long.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right, Barbara! Those antlers can get quite impressive — up to two feet long!
puzzle_1.close_response: Very close! Black-tailed deer antlers can grow up to about 24 inches long — that's two feet!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: These beautiful deer can grow antlers up to 24 inches long — quite impressive for our local deer!
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Black-tailed deer are found throughout the Pacific Northwest and are smaller than their mule deer cousins. Only the males (bucks) grow antlers, which they shed and regrow each year.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'thank you'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Köszönöm, Barbara — that's perfect! You know your Hungarian well!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word for 'thank you' is köszönöm! 'Szia' means 'hi' or 'bye,' 'igen' means 'yes,' and 'jó napot' means 'good day.'
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian is a unique language that's part of the Finno-Ugric family, making it quite different from most other European languages. It's known for its beautiful sounds and complex but logical grammar.

puzzle_3.question: Which flower is often called the 'Queen of the Garden'?
puzzle_3.correct_response: Beautifully done! The rose has been cherished for thousands of years and truly deserves its royal title as the Queen of the Garden.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: It's the rose! This beloved flower has been cultivated for over 5,000 years and appears in art, poetry, and gardens around the world.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Roses have been grown in gardens since ancient times, and there are now over 30,000 varieties. They come in almost every color except true blue, and many have the most wonderful fragrances.
